scope: 25 exact historical keys outside other assignments; original operators and endpoint scopes inspected. Full pages 327, 328, 334, 386 and 387 re-read for specific connections and qualifications.

rows.review_disposition: B888/6773 must preserve divided absolutist, constitutionalist and Orleanist tendencies and pragmatic electoral cooperation. Clichy organized metropolitan deputies and editors; it did not organize all monarchists in exile. Full 327–328 supports this narrower connection.

B319/3CBD must retain the Agency recovering direct taxes through commissioners. Full 334 does not make the central Agency simply a component of elected departmental administrations; distinguish fiscal centralization from the electoral/administrative hybrid described on 328.

7593/612D/4F5D/069F must retain émigré misjudgments, rivalry and dependence as contributors to failure. They are interacting causes across different episodes, not a claim that emigration itself invariably defeated every form of resistance.

3CA7/612D must preserve Puisaye’s exaggerated Breton military claims helping win support for Quiberon, followed by command and coordination failures. Retire an unqualified single-cause formulation while retaining the enabling misrepresentation.

43E0/60DA must preserve the Vendéan attempt to reach Granville and British linkage, including failed contact and incompatible expectations. Avoid treating the desired foreign aid as actually supplied in that operation.

3047/4F5D must retain the Lyonnais plotting link to Condé’s surviving army and the contingent wider scheme. A vague related-to edge may retire only with the concrete actors and planned connection retained.

48B/21A must preserve army dependence and military distrust preventing the constitutional experiment from testing plausible accommodation. Retain the author’s counterfactual caution: accommodation was possible, not certain.

B64/612D can preserve Île d’Yeu after Quiberon with the distinct failed landing, Artois’s hesitation and recall. Sequence does not make the second expedition identical to or an unavoidable consequence of the first.

29CD can internalize the survival of a substantial parliamentary opposition after Floréal. Preserve this limit on the purge alongside arbitrary invalidation; do not describe complete legislative elimination.

0848 can internalize Pius VII as indispensable negotiating party, pragmatic compatibility and acceptance of non-restoration of lands without legal endorsement of confiscation or Avignon’s annexation. Full 386–387 confirms negotiated compromise, not unilateral capitulation.

7593/612D/4F5D/9EDD may internalize émigrés as one component of counter-revolution. Preserve external action, its diversity and its overlap with internal allies without making all counter-revolution émigré-led.

0364/F4D/29CD must retain the triumvirs organizing the 1797 executive response. Their pre-Fructidor actions do not alone establish every later Second Directory measure, especially Floréal; keep event-specific responsibility.

2AC/71A and 571C must preserve civil rights for free people of colour preceding general emancipation, with changing eligibility, Ogé and colonial armed pressure. Temporal sequence does not imply consistent metropolitan universalism.

DA4B can internalize rapid land victories followed by naval isolation. Preserve the distinction between tactical success and strategic failure; the source’s departure-date discrepancy remains explicit.

621/1D983 must preserve Louis XVI’s execution, recognition of Louis XVII and the regency succession. 3ABA’s earlier Mirabeau advice is not itself evidence of that later dynastic sequence; do not spread the whole death-to-regency claim across every mapped parent.

A4EB/2FE1 must distinguish Rhine frontier incorporation and imperial compensation from establishing sister republics. Both express expansion, but annexation is not a subtype of satellite republican government.

B64/8EB must retain Artois as a principal actor in the failed Yeu landing, his failure to join the insurgents and subsequent departure. Correct evidence placement to 313 where required; 314 cannot bear every episode detail.
C455/888503 may internalize Jalès as southern Catholic royalism. AC7C’s particular Nîmes-to-Jalès mechanism is not identical to the broad inclusion relation; preserve both category and sequence.

381386 can internalize renewed émigré repression within the post-Fructidor programme, including deadlines and executions. Retire the unbound anti-royalist-repression node rather than make it a new independent requirement.

381386 must describe clerical coercion as part of the post-Fructidor repression, not simply an event that all Directorial Terror followed. Full 334 shows overlapping measures and an oath passed the day after the coup.
8689/60DA can internalize Charette’s leadership and distinct command within Vendéan resistance. Do not imply he led every phase or the entire Catholic and Royal Army without qualification.

Reject the reversed causal claim: tax collapse, visible debts and emergency sales preceded and helped prompt repudiation. FF3E must retain the financial emergency as context and the bankruptcy’s relief/costs as consequences.

7549/B888 must preserve localized, factional southern vengeance contrasted with coordinated electoral organization. Full 327–328 rejects a unified national royalist programme behind all White Terror killings.

BBD/9EDD must preserve the limits of royalist attribution to federalism and the distinction between opposing Parisian domination and seeking restoration. Later royalist opportunities do not erase federalist republican aims.

84FD/4F5D/3047 must retain Pichegru’s royalist contacts within the Lyonnais/Condé scheme, its dependence on military cooperation and uncertain feasibility. The separate vague linkage may retire with that concrete connection explicit.
